profile.reading:
DataBank LGA3 is a commercial colocation data center at 2000 Corporate Drive in Orangeburg, New York, in Rockland County's Hudson Valley, a location the operator markets for its proximity to New York City while sitting outside the city's flood, seismic, and hurricane storm-surge risk zones as an alternative or supplement to a Manhattan or New Jersey data hall. DataBank describes LGA3 as the third facility in its New York City metro portfolio.

Unlike most of the smaller telecom and enterprise-private facilities in this registry, DataBank is a wholesale and retail colocation operator that publishes real, current specifications for this building. As of this writing, LGA3 offers 110,000 square feet of built IT space with 20 megawatts of critical IT load in active service, with the full Orangeburg campus master-planned to grow to five data halls totaling 200,000 square feet and 40 megawatts once fully built out. Power distribution is designed to N+1 redundancy, offered in 120/208V and 240/415V AC configurations, and cooling is likewise N+1, supporting standard air-cooled cabinets above 35 kilowatts and liquid-cooled cabinets above 100 kilowatts, a specification aimed squarely at high-density AI and HPC colocation customers rather than only conventional enterprise racks. DataBank states the site has eight carriers available on-site with access to its interconnection marketplace, and it holds SOC 1 and SOC 2 attestations, HIPAA compliance, PCI DSS certification, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification. The operator also markets the site as running on 100 percent renewable-sourced energy with a 100 percent uptime service-level commitment.

DataBank itself was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Dallas, Texas. DigitalBridge, then known as Digital Bridge, acquired the company in July 2016 and built it into a national colocation platform through a long series of acquisitions. DataBank's own company history describes growth to more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. Trade press has reported that DigitalBridge later sold a stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management for roughly 1.2 billion dollars, though this has not been independently confirmed from a primary source for this record. LGA3 opened as part of that broader multi-market expansion, giving DataBank a purpose-built New York area campus rather than relying solely on acquired legacy buildings, and it reflects the company's more recent strategy of new-build development aimed at the AI-driven demand for higher power density that its N+1, liquid-cooling-capable design at LGA3 is explicitly built to serve.

reading.body:
DataBank LGA3 is a 20 megawatt colocation campus in Orangeburg, New York, built purpose-built for high-density AI and HPC workloads rather than converted from legacy enterprise infrastructure. The operator publishes specifications for both active and planned capacity: 110,000 square feet of IT space with 20 MW in service, growing to 200,000 square feet and 40 MW across five data halls once fully built. At typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the published 20 MW of IT load translates to roughly 500 racks in service today, with the master plan accommodating approximately 1,000 racks at full build-out.

The campus design targets AI tenancy directly: N+1 redundancy on both power and cooling, 120/208V and 240/415V AC distribution, and explicit support for liquid-cooled cabinets above 100 kilowatts per unit. Eight carriers provide on-site interconnection, and the operator claims SOC 1, SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certifications, qualifying the facility for regulated enterprise and hyperscaler workloads. DataBank markets the site as running on 100 percent renewable energy and offers a 100 percent uptime service-level agreement, though neither claim is independently verified in this record.

LGA3 is the largest data center campus by published capacity in New York State, where only one facility of 31 mapped reports any megawatt figure to public specification. It sits in the Hudson Valley outside New York City flood, seismic, and hurricane zones, positioning it as geographic redundancy for Manhattan and New Jersey colocation. The campus remains under active expansion and represents DataBank's strategy of new-build development for AI-driven demand, distinct from the company's earlier growth through acquisition of legacy facilities.
